title: Google Ends Local NDA Requirements for Data Center Construction

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Municipal leaders will no longer be required to sign confidentiality contracts before discussing the build-out of new facilities with Google. The company has removed the requirement for local officials to enter into nondisclosure agreements during the planning of its data centers, a policy shift first reported by The Information.

The move aligns Google with Microsoft and Amazon, both of which previously abandoned the use of secrecy deals for similar infrastructure projects. Transparency advocates have frequently criticized these agreements, arguing they prevent the public from seeing the full terms, tax incentives, and costs of data center developments.
